court_name: Superior Court of California, County of San Francisco
case_search_note: Criminal case portal (linked from sf.courts.ca.gov/online-services/case-information): search by case number, defendant name or attorney name; shows calendar and register of actions. Per CRC 2.503(c) criminal documents cannot be viewed or downloaded remotely — request copies from the Criminal Clerk, Hall of Justice Room 101. A Cumulative Criminal Index (updated weekly) is at https://webapps.sftc.org/crimindex/crimindex.dll. Upcoming hearings by date: Case Calendars search at webapps.sftc.org/cc/CaseCalendar.dll.

courthouses.name: Hall of Justice
courthouses.hours: Building Mon–Fri 8:30 a.m.–4:00 p.m. Criminal Division (Room 101) phone hours 8:30 a.m.–4:00 p.m., closed 12–1 p.m. and holidays.
courthouses.note: All adult criminal cases: felony and misdemeanor arraignments, preliminary hearings, trials, collaborative courts (Dept. 15 Behavioral Health Court/Mental Health Diversion, Dept. 24 Veterans Justice Court). Criminal Clerk Room 101 (415) 551-0651, fax (415) 551-8085. Traffic Division Room 145 (415) 551-8540. A court notice dated 2026-08-14 proposes reduced clerk's-office hours (8:30 a.m.–12:30 p.m. with drop boxes after) — confirm hours before going. Department list from Judicial Assignments 2026; assignments rotate.

courthouses.name: Civic Center Courthouse
courthouses.hours: Building open to the public Mon–Fri 8:15 a.m.–5:00 p.m.; filing clerk offices (Rooms 103 and 402) 8:30 a.m.–4:00 p.m., closed 12–1 p.m.
courthouses.note: Civil, Unified Family Court, Traffic and the ACCESS (Legal Self-Help) Center (415) 551-0605. The court's page lists a Traffic Division line (415) 551-8550 here; no criminal division is listed.

courthouses.name: Juvenile Justice Center
courthouses.note: Juvenile justice (delinquency) and juvenile traffic only — not adult criminal. Juvenile Hall and Juvenile Probation are in the same complex.

legal_aid.serves: Anyone seeking a private attorney in San Francisco
legal_aid.what: Referrals to private lawyers, including Criminal Law. Free or reduced-cost services for those who qualify. Phone lines weekdays 9:00 a.m.–1:00 p.m. and 1:30–4:30 p.m. No walk-ins.

San Francisco Juvenile Probation Department

programs.name: San Francisco Pretrial Diversion Project (pretrial release & diversion)
programs.summary: Nonprofit that runs San Francisco's pretrial release and diversion programs: judges may release recently arrested people to its supervision; offers court-date reminders, outreach/escorts to court, and links to behavioral health, benefits and housing. Your release order sets your conditions.
programs.todo: Program-by-program details (sfpretrial.org/what-we-do/our-programs/) not loaded. Office: 1200 Folsom St (at 8th St).

programs.name: Behavioral Health Court
programs.summary: For people with serious, persistent mental illness; supports reintegration and self-sufficiency. Judicial Assignments 2026 list it in Dept. 15, Hall of Justice.

programs.name: Mental Health Diversion
programs.summary: Statutory pretrial diversion for people with an eligible DSM-5 mental health diagnosis, with individualized clinical treatment. Dept. 15, Hall of Justice per Judicial Assignments 2026.

programs.name: Community Justice Center
programs.summary: Restorative justice and treatment-focused court for cases from the Tenderloin, Civic Center, Union Square and South of Market.
programs.todo: Current location/department not stated on the collaborative courts page

programs.name: Drug Court
programs.summary: Links nonviolent defendants with substance use disorders to outpatient or residential treatment.

programs.name: Veterans Justice Court
programs.summary: For veterans facing criminal charges; social service, education and vocational support. Dept. 24, Hall of Justice per Judicial Assignments 2026.

programs.name: Young Adult Court
programs.summary: For transitional-age adults 18–25, including some violent cases.

programs.name: Intensive Supervision Court
programs.summary: For high-risk, high-needs probationers as a last chance at community supervision instead of state prison.

programs.name: ACCESS (Legal Self-Help) Center
programs.summary: Court self-help center at the Civic Center Courthouse, 400 McAllister St. Phone and in-person help limited to Monday, Tuesday and Thursday mornings.

jails.name: Intake and Release Center
jails.phone_note: Mon–Fri 8 a.m.–5 p.m.; all other times incl. weekends/holidays (415) 553-1444. Booking after arrest; no visits here.

jails.name: County Jail #2
jails.phone_note: Mon–Fri 8 a.m.–5 p.m.; other times incl. weekends/holidays (415) 553-1444. Visit scheduling (415) 553-1430 or sf.gtlvisitme.com/app. Up to 392 people.
jails.todo: Sheriff says CJ#2 is the only SF jail that houses women; whether it also houses men is not stated. court_ids = nearest criminal courthouse, not confirmed.

jails.name: County Jail #3 (formerly County Jail #5)
jails.phone_note: Located in San Bruno (San Mateo County) but run by the SF Sheriff. Largest SF jail, up to 768 people. Flywheel visitor transport: (855) 359-2420. Visit scheduling (415) 553-1430 or sf.gtlvisitme.com/app. Cash-only deposit kiosk for registered visitors during visiting hours.
jails.todo: No direct phone on the jail's page. houses='men' is inferred from the Sheriff saying CJ#2 is the only jail that houses women. court_ids = SF's only adult criminal courthouse, transport not confirmed.

jails.name: San Francisco Juvenile Hall
jails.phone_note: Juvenile Probation Department main line; front desk takes questions about arrests, court hearings, probation or Juvenile Hall.
jails.todo: Visiting rules page not located. Same complex as the Juvenile Justice Center courthouse.

bail.note: CA Department of Insurance 'Check a License' — look up a bail agent's license status by name or license number. The SF Sheriff's site has no page explaining where or how to post cash bail (checked jail services, Getting released, Intake & Release Center pages on 2026-10-13); call the Intake & Release Center at (415) 558-4443 (weekdays 8–5) or (415) 553-1444 (other times). The 24-hour lobby kiosks at 425 7th Street are for inmate account deposits, not bail.
